description: City considers converting 0.34 acres of Dundonald Park for Fire Station 10.
Internal funds transfer of $300,000 for land and levies.

chips.text: First reading passed (10-0)
10 for, 0 against
Councillor Davies supports proposal, citing five years of risk for delayed response times.
Residents of Dundonald Park, Hampton Village, Kensington, and Elk Point are affected.
Future fire station planning will involve earlier engagement in sector plans.
No data provided on fire station impact on property values in other neighborhoods.
Residents expressed strong opposition due to safety, noise, traffic, and loss of green space.
Noise from sirens could trigger students with auditory sensitivities at Dundonald School.
Public concerned about loss of green space; city promises tree replacement.

speakers.name: Chief Wegren
speakers.summary: Chief Wegren, Saskatoon Fire Department, presented the report with a PowerPoint.
said: New station improves response times in northwest Saskatoon.
Current response times exceed 1710 standard in northwest.
Proposed site offers optimal 360-degree emergency coverage.

description: Approves a gas bar and convenience store on Parcel Q.
Located at Ferraguesi Boulevard and Orban Way, Aspen Ridge.
Includes six fuel pumps and underground fuel tanks.

chips.text: Approved
9 for, 0 against
Administration explained why gas bars are discretionary in B4MX zoning.
Property owners within 150 meters of Parcel Q were notified.
Public raised concerns about environmental contamination, traffic, and residential impact.

description: Permits a commercial school for 12 students at 415 Willowgrove Square.
The school will offer art and hobby instruction.

chips.text: Approved
9 for, 0 against
Councillor Declan questioned administration's focus on land use over specific school type.
Residents of Willow Grove neighborhood raised parking and traffic concerns.

description: Approves a daycare for 45 children, 10 staff.

chips.text: Approved
9 for, 0 against
Applicant argued 45 children allows for better programming and staff benefits.
Rosewood residents raised concerns about increased traffic and noise.
Council approved the daycare despite administration's recommendation for denial.
A resident warned this approval sets a precedent for residential lots becoming commercial.
Questions about future enforcement of capacity limits and parking overflow remained unanswered.
The daycare provides crucial support for children with additional needs and their families.
Applicant promised to prioritize Rosewood families and mitigate traffic and noise impacts.

description: Re-designates 1701 Idylwyld Drive North from light industrial to institutional.
Allows permanent operation of a complex needs emergency shelter.

chips.text: First reading passed (9-0)
9 for, 0 against
Staff confirmed 15-bed limit for shelter; any increase requires bylaw amendment.
Nearby business owner and resident reported increased crime and vandalism.
Role of facility in province's involuntary commitment plans is still undetermined.
Public speakers raised concerns about increased crime and lack of support systems.
Shelter serves people experiencing long-term homelessness, complex health conditions, and trauma.

description: Allows a 15-resident special care home at 1701 Idylwyld North.

chips.text: First reading passed (9-0)
9 for, 0 against
Businesses and residents near 1701 Idylwyld North are affected.
Public concern that approving this rezoning sets a precedent.
Public delegate stated area businesses oppose the rezoning.

description: Removes holding symbol from 3950 Idylwyld Drive North.
Developer paid $7.69 million for wetland loss.
Funds will restore or enhance other city wetlands.

chips.text: Approved
9 for, 0 against
Councillor Kelleher asked about the specific environmental impact of losing the wetlands.
York Realty Inc. is the developer for the industrial site.
Financial compensation for wetland loss was used in past projects.
Specific environmental impacts of wetland loss were not detailed by staff.
Matt Woolsey of York Realty introduced his company and its industrial development focus.
Loss of 13.87 hectares of wetlands will be compensated financially.
